channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches '1000 Genomes' Project to Study Population Genetics
item.description: Uzbekistan's Center for Advanced Technologies has initiated the '1000 Genomes' project, collecting blood samples to study the genetic characteristics of its population and create a national database. The project aims to identify prevalent gene variants for future diagnostic tests and treatments, with plans to collect 3000 samples by 2028.

item.title: Russia to Introduce Additional Tax for Migrants with Non-Working Family Members
item.description: Starting in 2027, Russia will implement additional financial obligations for labor migrants accompanied by non-working family members, primarily affecting those with minor children. The measure aims to reduce the burden on the social sphere by increasing the fixed advance tax payment for patent holders by 50% per dependent child.

item.title: Uzbekistan Amends Urbanization Code to Improve Governance and Living Conditions
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing public administration in urbanization, focusing on creating comfortable living environments and improving urban development. A new bill, discussed in the Legislative Chamber, aims to regulate these processes by defining key principles for urban planning, including economic development, quality of life, and environmental improvement. The legislation also clarifies the roles of national committees in sustainable urbanization and housing.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Speaker Meets with South Korean President
item.description: Tanzila Narbayeva, Speaker of the Senate of Uzbekistan, met with the President of South Korea. The discussion focused on strengthening inter-parliamentary relations, developing strategic partnerships, and expanding cooperation on prospective projects and technology. The meeting aimed to enhance bilateral ties between the two nations.

item.title: Criminal case opened against Turkish oligarch's company over gold mine investment in East Kazakhstan
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in the East Kazakhstan region concerning alleged fraud involving the Mankа gold mine. The case targets a company owned by Turkish businessman Robert Yildirim, Yildirim Holding, which entered the Kazakh market in 2013. The investigation is ongoing and under the supervision of the Prosecutor General's Office.

item.title: Farhodjon Sharipov appointed Deputy Governor of Bukhara region, heading investment and industry
item.description: Farhodjon Sharipov has been appointed as the Deputy Governor of the Bukhara region, responsible for investments, industry, and trade. He previously served as the deputy head of the investment, industry, and trade department in the Bukhara district. Sharipov graduated from Bukhara State University with a degree in economics.

item.title: Bishkek Smog Linked to Heating and Vehicle Emissions, Officials Say
item.description: Bishkek faces severe air pollution due to coal heating and vehicle emissions. 58 residential areas lack gas, while 700,000 cars operate on roads designed for 300,000. Authorities are installing air quality monitoring stations and improving fuel quality control to combat the issue.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ex-President's Daughter Helps Uncover Underground Dog Fighting Ring
item.description: Aliya Shagieva, daughter of Kyrgyzstan's ex-president, aided authorities in dismantling an underground dog fighting network. She gathered evidence, including recorded conversations detailing brutal fights ending in canine death. The suspect, allegedly operating across all seven regions, was detained.

item.title: Iran Claims Two Tankers Stopped in Strait of Hormuz After Explosions
item.description: Iran's IRGC Navy reported that two "violating" oil tankers were stopped in the Strait of Hormuz following explosions. One supertanker allegedly hit a sea mine, while the second, reportedly under US military escort, also caught fire. Both vessels were abandoned burning.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Bank Proposes Changes to Installment Plans
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank is not planning to restrict access to installment plans, according to Deputy Chairman Vitaly Tutushkin. The regulator aims to increase market transparency and establish minimum consumer protection requirements, focusing on contract disclosure rather than price or volume controls. Proposed changes consider the interests of all parties involved.

item.title: Kazakhstan Postpones Film Premiere on Chingiz Aitmatov Amid Censorship Reports
item.description: The premiere of a biographical film about Kyrgyz writer Chingiz Aitmatov in Kazakhstan has been postponed from November 12 to December 3. While creators cited unspecified circumstances, critics suggest the delay may be linked to censorship issues faced by the film in Russia, where scenes about Stalinist repressions were reportedly removed.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Truck driver rams police during illegal sand extraction raid
item.description: In Uzbekistan's Samarkand region, a truck driver resisted eco-police during a raid on illegal sand extraction. The driver endangered officers and damaged their vehicle while attempting to help an excavator escape. Authorities are assessing environmental damage and will transfer materials to law enforcement.

item.title: Aitmatov Film Faces Censorship in Russia, Premiere Postponed in Kazakhstan
item.description: The film 'Aitmatov' is embroiled in a censorship controversy. A scene depicting the execution of the writer's father during Stalin's repressions was cut from the Russian version. Meanwhile, the film's premiere in Kazakhstan, initially set for November 12, has been indefinitely postponed.

item.title: Yandex Cloud Recovers 97% of Data After Drone Attacks, Some Data Lost Irreversibly
item.description: Yandex Cloud has restored access to 97.16% of client data following drone attacks on Russian data centers. The remaining 2.84% is lost due to critical equipment damage and lack of user backups. Yandex has since made backups automatic for new virtual machines and is diversifying infrastructure.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tenge Overvalued by 20%, Gradual Weakening Expected
item.description: Analysts at BCC Invest believe Kazakhstan's tenge is currently 20% stronger than fundamental economic factors justify. They anticipate a gradual weakening of the currency to 480 tenge per dollar. The tenge's real exchange rate has appreciated significantly faster than economic indicators over the past year, driven by foreign capital inflows, high oil prices, and substantial state currency sales.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Seeks Second Term in Upcoming Elections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has submitted documents to the Central Election Commission to run for a second term. He is participating as an independent candidate. Japarov previously won the early presidential elections on January 10, 2021, with 79.2% of the vote. The next presidential election is scheduled for January 27, 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Grew 4.5% in January-October 2026, Slower Than Previous Year
item.description: Kazakhstan's economy expanded by 4.5% in January-October 2026, a slowdown from 6.4% in the same period last year. Manufacturing and construction were key growth drivers, despite an 8.3% drop in oil production. Household incomes saw minimal increase after accounting for inflation in the first half of the year.

item.title: Qatar Continues Efforts to Resolve US-Iran Crisis, Citing Positive Responses
item.description: Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced ongoing mediation efforts to resolve uncertainties in the US-Iran crisis. A ministry official stated both sides have responded positively to Qatar's initiatives. The approaching winter and potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz have reportedly doubled crisis-related costs.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Elevate Strategic Partnership During Parliamentary Visit
item.description: A parliamentary delegation from Uzbekistan, led by Senate Chairwoman Tanzila Narbaeva, is on an official visit to South Korea. Meetings with President Lee Jae-myung highlighted the deepening strategic partnership, focusing on projects worth nearly $12 billion, innovation, new production capacities, and inter-regional ties. Cooperation in education, medicine, and science was also discussed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Scraps Fine for Illegal Construction Per Square Meter
item.description: Uzbekistan has abandoned plans to introduce a fine of five basic calculation units (2.2 million soums) per square meter for illegal construction. The provision was removed from a draft amendment to the Urban Development Code during its final review. A separate law passed in September already increased penalties for construction violations, including criminal liability for repeated offenses.

item.title: Karzai Urges Reopening of Schools and Universities to Girls in Afghanistan
item.description: Former Afghan President Hamid Karzai has reiterated his call for the swift reopening of schools and universities to girls, emphasizing education's crucial role in national development and independence. He stressed that progress and prosperity depend on educational opportunities for all citizens. Since the Taliban's takeover, millions of girls have been denied secondary education.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host 'Tajikistan-2026' Exhibition with Participants from Eight Countries
item.description: The international universal exhibition 'Tajikistan-2026' will be held from November 12-14 in Dushanbe. Organized by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Tajikistan, it will feature products and services from Tajikistan, Russia, Belarus, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Iran, Pakistan, and China. The event aims to help companies find business partners.

item.title: Uzbek-Russian Media Forum Continues in Tashkent
item.description: The third Uzbek-Russian media forum is underway in Tashkent, organized by Uzbekistan's National Information Agency (UzA) and Russia's TASS news agency. Participants are discussing information cooperation, joint media projects, and promoting cultural heritage through media. Topics include information exchange, film production, and AI in media.

item.title: China Approves Fresh Kyrgyz Berry Exports, Expanding Agricultural Trade
item.description: China has granted approval for the import of fresh raspberries, blackcurrants, and blackberries from Kyrgyzstan. This decision, announced on October 20, follows a plant health agreement signed in August. The move could offer Kyrgyz berry growers new markets beyond Russia and Kazakhstan, although strawberries are not included in the current agreement.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts Escrow System for Shared Housing Construction
item.description: Uzbekistan is progressively implementing an escrow system for shared housing construction, with funds to be transferred to developers only after property handover. This initiative, discussed in the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis, aims to enhance legal guarantees for citizens' funds. The system will become mandatory for all shared construction projects starting January 1, 2026.

item.title: Outdated Standards Hinder Uzbekistan's WTO Accession, Say Deputies
item.description: Deputies in Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber have issued a parliamentary inquiry regarding outdated technical regulations and standards. Approximately 50% of the current 33,000 standards do not meet international requirements, hindering the country's accession to the World Trade Organization. Concerns were also raised about insufficient digitalization and corruption risks within the sector.

item.title: Almaty Road Development Agency Faces Abuse of Power Investigation
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee is investigating alleged abuse of power within Almaty's Road Development Agency. The city prosecutor's office uncovered violations, including the payment of 202 million tenge for a project documentation that failed state expertise and was unusable. Penalties were not enforced for a 27 million tenge contract.

item.title: Kazakhstan Telecom Investment Exceeds $2.2 Billion, Rural Connectivity Lags
item.description: Kazakhstan's telecom sector investment surpassed $2.2 billion in three years, yet only 2,606 of 6,179 villages have fiber-optic backbone access. The government aims for over 90% of villages to have high-speed internet by end of 2027. A World Bank project supports local network construction in 1,123 villages for 445,000 households.

item.title: Seven Charged in Connection with Deaths of Three Teenagers in Kazakhstan's Korday District
item.description: Pre-trial investigation into the bullying and subsequent deaths of three minors in Korday district, Zhambyl region, has concluded. Authorities reported that seven individuals are being prosecuted. Two suspects face charges of extortion and incitement to suicide and have been detained. Five others are charged with extortion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Oil Pipeline Expansion to China, Raising Questions About Russian Interests
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to expand its oil pipeline system to China, primarily to supply the Shymkent refinery. However, more Russian oil is transported through this pipeline to China than Kazakh oil. Kazakhstan plans to borrow funds for the expansion, prompting questions about the project's beneficiaries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ski Resorts Prepare for Winter Season with Safety Inspections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's ski resorts are gearing up for the upcoming winter tourist season. Journalists visited the "Chun-Kurčak" and "ZiL" ski bases to observe preparations, including checks on cable car readiness and infrastructure. The Ministry of Natural Resources' Environmental and Technical Supervision Service conducted inspections to ensure compliance with safety regulations and operational standards.

item.title: Almaty Court Overturns Acquittal in Sunkar Ski Jumps Embezzlement Case
item.description: An appellate court in Almaty has overturned an acquittal verdict for Yerlan Sariev in the embezzlement case related to the construction of the "Sunkar" ski jumps complex. The court partially granted the prosecutor's motion and the victims' representatives' appeals. Sariev's pre-trial measure of house arrest was maintained, and the case will be reconsidered from the first instance.

item.title: Activists in Germany Urge Court Not to Forget Dilmurod Ergashev's Fate
item.description: A group of activists and human rights defenders in Germany held a protest urging the Düsseldorf court not to be indifferent to the fate of Tajik activist Dilmurod Ergashev. Ergashev was deported from Germany to Tajikistan in November 2024 and sentenced to eight years in prison for allegedly inciting extremism. The court is reviewing the legality of his deportation.

item.title: Head of Kyrgyzstan's State Property Management Agency Discusses Corruption
item.description: Beksultan Tokonov, Director of Kyrgyzstan's State Agency for Property Management (SAUM), stated that individuals are not born corrupt but become so due to their environment, leadership's illegal orders, and starting from the lowest ranks. He praised the current leadership for not issuing unlawful directives and emphasized that a modern manager's key quality is their attitude towards people, not just professional skills.

item.title: Almaty Activist Nazym Tabyldieva Sentenced to 5 Days Administrative Arrest
item.description: An Almaty court has sentenced activist Nazym Tabyldieva to five days of administrative detention for violating a court-imposed restriction. Tabyldieva was found guilty of breaching a 2021 sentence that limited her freedom and prohibited her from engaging in public activities or posting on social media. Her lawyer plans to appeal the decision.

item.title: US Dollar Trades at 447.22 Tenge on Kazakhstan Stock Exchange
item.description: The average weighted exchange rate of the US dollar on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange decreased by 1.60 tenge, closing at 447.22 tenge after Tuesday's trading session. The national currency strengthened against the dollar during the trading day.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Bank Issues 10 Billion Tenge in Tokenized Notes
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has issued short-term notes totaling 50 billion tenge, with 10 billion tenge in tokenized form. The placement occurred on the KASE digital asset platform, marking a practical step in integrating digital financial assets into the government securities market. The notes have a 91-day term.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes New Border Bridge and End to 'Re-coupling' Mechanism with Turkmenistan
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed constructing a new, high-capacity bridge over the Yomojar canal at the 'Olot' border crossing with Turkmenistan, replacing the outdated 1978 structure. Uzbekistan also seeks to abandon the 're-coupling' mechanism, introduced by Turkmenistan during the pandemic, to streamline international freight transport and reduce border procedures.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Extortion Case Among Schoolchildren Leading to Three Teen Suicides Goes to Court
item.description: In Kazakhstan's Zhambyl region, an investigation into an extortion scheme among schoolchildren, allegedly leading to the suicides of three minors, has concluded. The prosecution states evidence points to a causal link between the extortion and the deaths. Two suspects face charges of extortion and incitement to suicide.

item.title: CSTO Security Officials Discuss Threats and Adopt Decisions in Moscow
item.description: Adilet Orozbekov, Secretary of the Security Council of Kyrgyzstan, attended a joint meeting of CSTO foreign ministers, defense ministers, and security council secretaries in Moscow. They discussed cooperation on responding to threats to collective security and adopted decisions to improve the organization's activities. This meeting is a final important stage before the next session of the CSTO Collective Security Council on November 11, 2026.
